fact_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s flagship model had a 3.9% failure rate in the 55 °C sustained-heat test
a thermal-incident rate of 9.9 per 100,000 installed units last year
Northwind’s Hearth 10 had a 6.2% failure rate in the 55 °C test
6.4 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year
Halcyon recorded 8.1 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units company-wide last year
Four thermal incidents were not reported to a regulator

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any battery-related fire, thermal runaway, or injury to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, and provide a fuller incident report within 10 calendar days. Other thermal incidents requiring emergency services or causing property damage must be reported within 5 calendar days. The manufacturer must notify affected customers within 72 hours of determining that their unit or model may present a material safety risk, with immediate instructions for urgent hazards.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and a representative sample. Manufacturers must provide per-model protocols, sample sizes, and results to the responsible regulator and to customers who buy that model, in clear and accessible form; individual-company, per-model results need not be published to the general public. A failure rate above 5% requires prompt regulator notification, investigation, and a corrective-action plan, including retesting under regulator oversight. The regulator may require additional risk controls or restrict a model where the evidence indicates unacceptable risk; exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit sale.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New battery systems must support secure remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized access and clear customer instructions. Manufacturers must provide a retrofit plan for installed units and complete retrofits, where technically feasible, within 6 years of the standard taking effect. If a retrofit is infeasible or would create a greater safety risk, the manufacturer must notify the regulator and provide an equivalent mitigation plan.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New battery systems must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after the standard is adopted. Manufacturers must provide the regulator with evidence that the suppression system is appropriate for the battery design and does not introduce a greater safety risk.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator, investigate the causes, and submit a corrective-action plan. The regulator must promptly assess the incident severity and other available evidence and may require a recall, including an immediate recall where warranted. A manufacturer must promptly notify affected customers and provide clear recall and corrective instructions when a recall is required. A manufacturer must notify affected customers within 72 hours after determining that a unit or model may present a material safety risk, with immediate instructions for urgent hazards.

section_notes.S1_incident_reporting: Serious incidents must be reported within 24 hours and other emergency/property-damage incidents within 5 days. Customer notice is within 72 hours, but minor overheating/smoke without emergency services or property damage is not reportable, which weakens scope.
section_notes.S2_thermal_testing: Testing is at 55 °C, and results go to regulators and purchasers but not the general public. A failure rate above 5% triggers corrective action and regulator oversight, but does not automatically stop sales, leaving an open-ended above-limit sales window.
section_notes.S3_remote_shutoff: New units must support remote shut-off from adoption. Retrofits for installed units are required within 6 years, with a feasibility escape that requires an equivalent mitigation plan.
section_notes.S4_fire_suppression: Built-in fire suppression is required for new units beginning 36 months after adoption. No validated equivalent is allowed.
section_notes.S5_customer_disclosure: The 8 per 100,000 threshold triggers regulator notification, investigation, and a corrective-action plan, but recall is discretionary with the regulator. Safety notices to affected customers are due within 72 hours.
